text: The LORD reigns! Let the earth rejoice; let the many coastlands be glad.

versions.text: The LORD reigns! Let the earth rejoice; let the many islands be glad.
versions.explanation: אִיִּים in this context refers to distant coastlands/shores, evoking the far reaches of the inhabited world rather than islands specifically; "coastlands" is the more precise sense.

text: Cloud and thick darkness surround him; righteousness and justice are the foundation of his throne.
Fire goes before him and consumes his foes on every side.
His lightning flashes light up the world; the earth sees and trembles.

versions.text: His lightning lights up the world; the earth sees it and trembles.
versions.explanation: "lightning lights" repeats the same root sound awkwardly for oral reading; the Hebrew בְרָקָיו is plural ("his lightnings/flashes"). Dropping "it" also matches the compact Hebrew ("the earth saw and writhed").

text: The mountains melt like wax before the LORD, before the Lord of all the earth.
The heavens proclaim his righteousness, and all the peoples see his glory.
Let all who serve carved images be put to shame, all who boast in worthless idols. Bow down before him, all you gods!

versions.text: All who serve carved images are put to shame, those who boast in worthless idols. All you gods, bow down before him!
versions.explanation: The imperfect יֵבֹשׁוּ stands in parallel with the following imperative ("bow down"), so a jussive rendering ("Let... be put to shame") better matches the volitional force of the verse and reads with stronger rhythm.

versions.text: Let all who serve carved images be put to shame, all who boast in worthless idols.
versions.explanation: The final clause of the Hebrew, הִשְׁתַּחֲווּ־לוֹ כָּל־אֱלֹהִים ("Bow down before him, all you gods"), is missing from the current text. It was present in the previous revision and must be restored; the jussive rendering of the opening verb is retained as intended.

text: Zion hears and is glad, and the daughters of Judah rejoice because of your judgments, O LORD.
For you, O LORD, are the Most High over all the earth; you are exalted far above all gods.
You who love the LORD, hate evil! He guards the lives of his faithful ones; he rescues them from the hand of the wicked.
Light is sown for the righteous, and joy for the upright in heart.

Rejoice in the LORD, you righteous, and give thanks to his holy name.
[Footnote: Literally "to the remembrance of his holiness"; the phrase points to God's name as that by which he is remembered.]

versions.text: Rejoice in the LORD, you righteous, and give thanks to his holy name.
versions.explanation: The rendering is acceptable, but לְזֵכֶר קָדְשׁוֹ literally means "to the memorial/remembrance of his holiness"; a brief footnote preserves the imagery without disturbing the smooth reading text.
